column1: # lemma | pos | tgt | tgt2 | gender | ipa | etymon | note
# tgt   citation form: singular noun, infinitive verb, masculine
#       singular adjective, nominative singular for Latin/Old English.
# tgt2  plural for nouns, the gerund for verbs (dicendo). A blank tgt2 on
#       a noun means the English plural is never woven, which is the
#       correct outcome: weaving a singular target under an English
#       plural teaches a form that does not exist.
# gender m or f, and printed under both forms, so a noun whose plural takes
#       the other gender is woven in the singular only. osso, braccio, dito,
#       uovo and orecchio are masculine, and the plurals English means by
#       bones, arms, fingers, eggs and ears are feminine: ossa, braccia, dita,
#       uova, orecchie. The masculine plurals English Wiktionary gives four of
#       them are figurative or of the parts one at a time. orecchio was marked
#       neuter until 2026-10-08, a gender Italian does not have.
